instruction: Create research proposals for automatic validation of retrieval-augmented generation pipelines. The proposals should improve beyond simple answer-level LLM judging and should be feasible to evaluate on small QA benchmarks.
bit: Most RAG evaluation pipelines rely on final answer correctness or generic LLM-as-a-judge scores, which makes it difficult to locate whether failures come from retrieval, grounding, synthesis, or citation behavior. This limits reproducibility because different judges may reward polished answers even when evidence use is weak.

reference_papers.title: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
ARES: An Automated Evaluation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
TruLens: Tracking and Evaluating LLM Experiments

literature_context: Current RAG eval work commonly separates retrieval quality, faithfulness, answer relevance, and context precision. A useful proposer should suggest a concrete method with datasets, failure labels, ablations, and small-scale reproducible metrics.

instruction: Propose a method to adapt an English-centric LLM to Russian more efficiently than full supervised fine-tuning. The idea should include datasets, baselines, metrics, and ablations.
bit: Standard supervised fine-tuning for language adaptation updates many parameters on broad instruction data, which can be expensive and can degrade general capabilities. For Russian, the cost is amplified by tokenization inefficiency and limited high-quality domain-balanced instruction data.

reference_papers.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
Vocabulary Adaptation for Efficient Language Model Transfer

literature_context: Relevant directions include tokenizer adaptation, adapter methods, bilingual replay, synthetic instruction generation, and measuring both Russian task gains and English retention.

instruction: Generate research proposals for improving cold-start recommendation beyond common metadata-based and popularity-based baselines. Focus on feasible experiments with public datasets.
bit: Cold-start recommendation often falls back to content metadata, demographic priors, or popularity, which helps coverage but poorly captures early user intent and item-specific uncertainty. These approaches usually treat the first interactions as sparse static evidence rather than an active process for learning useful preference signals.

reference_papers.title: LightGCN: Simplifying and Powering Graph Convolution Network for Recommendation
DropoutNet: Addressing Cold Start in Recommender Systems
Meta-Learning for User Cold-Start Recommendation

literature_context: A strong proposal should specify user/item cold-start splits, baselines such as popularity, content KNN, matrix factorization, LightGCN variants, and metrics such as Recall@K and NDCG@K.

instruction: Propose a novel pipeline for using LLMs in neural architecture search for time series forecasting or classification. Include baselines, datasets, metrics, and ablations.
bit: Time-series NAS methods often search over fixed cell spaces or manually designed temporal blocks, while LLM-based architecture generation can produce invalid or expensive candidates without domain-specific constraints. This creates a gap between creative architecture proposals and feasible, comparable time-series experiments.

reference_papers.title: PatchTST: A Time Series is Worth 64 Words
iTransformer: Inverted Transformers Are Effective for Time Series Forecasting
DARTS: Differentiable Architecture Search
FunSearch: Making New Discoveries in Mathematical Sciences using Large Language Models

literature_context: Useful evaluations include ETTh1, ETTh2, Weather, ECL, Traffic, and UCR classification datasets. Baselines should include manual SOTA, random search, classical NAS, and direct LLM generation.

instruction: Create research proposals for evaluating and improving observability in multi-agent LLM research systems. Focus on failure attribution and benchmarkable metrics.
bit: Multi-agent LLM systems often log raw messages and tool calls, but failure attribution remains manual because traces do not map cleanly to agent responsibilities, task states, or recoverable error categories. This makes it hard to compare orchestration strategies or prove that observability changes improve research outcomes.

reference_papers.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
Langfuse Observability for LLM Applications
OpenTelemetry: A Framework for Observability

literature_context: A useful proposal should define trace-derived metrics, synthetic failure injection, human or LLM adjudication for attribution quality, and ablations over trace schema granularity.

instruction: Propose a method for improving controllability of diffusion models when generating structured outputs (e.g. molecules, layouts, or code). Provide datasets, baselines, metrics, and ablations.
bit: Diffusion models excel at unconditional or weakly conditional generation but struggle to honor hard structural constraints. Classifier-free guidance and post-hoc projection either drift the sample distribution or break differentiability, which limits use in domains where validity is required at every step.

reference_papers.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
Classifier-Free Diffusion Guidance
Score-Based Generative Modeling Through Stochastic Differential Equations
DiffDock: Diffusion Steps, Twists, and Turns for Molecular Docking

literature_context: Useful proposals should define a structural validity metric, compare against classifier-free guidance and projection baselines on at least one constrained domain (molecules, code, or layouts), and report both fidelity and constraint-satisfaction rate.

instruction: Propose a method to improve discrete vector quantization (VQ) for large-scale representation learning. The method should reduce codebook collapse and improve downstream linear probing accuracy.
bit: Standard VQ-VAE suffers from codebook collapse and dead codes, where most inputs map to a small subset of vectors. Common workarounds (EMA updates, codebook resets) help but do not address the underlying mismatch between encoder gradients and discrete assignment.

reference_papers.title: Neural Discrete Representation Learning (VQ-VAE)
Generating Diverse High-Fidelity Images with VQ-VAE-2
Finite Scalar Quantization: VQ-VAE Made Simple
Self-Supervised Learning of Visual Features with Codebook Quantization

literature_context: A strong proposal should specify codebook utilization metrics, compare against VQ-VAE, FSQ, and EMA-VQ on ImageNet linear probing, and provide ablations on codebook size and commitment loss weight.

topic: Scalable GNN training on large graphs
instruction: Propose a training method for graph neural networks that scales to graphs with >100M nodes while preserving the accuracy of full-graph message passing.
bit: Full-batch GNN training does not scale beyond a few million nodes due to memory. Standard subgraph sampling (GraphSAGE, Cluster-GCN) introduces variance and breaks long-range dependencies, leading to a measurable accuracy drop on heterophilic and long-range tasks.

reference_papers.title: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs (GraphSAGE)
Cluster-GCN: An Efficient Algorithm for Training Deep and Large Graph Convolutional Networks
Graph Attention Networks
Long Range Graph Benchmark

literature_context: A useful proposal should define a measurable accuracy gap vs full-batch on at least one long-range benchmark, propose a scalable training scheme with bounded memory, and ablate sampling/communication choices.

instruction: Propose a sequential recommendation method that performs well when most users have fewer than 10 interactions, with public datasets, baselines, metrics, and ablations.
bit: Sequential recommenders such as SASRec and BERT4Rec assume long interaction sequences and degrade sharply on short-history users, which dominate real catalogs. Augmentation and contrastive objectives help but typically improve dense regimes more than sparse ones.

reference_papers.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation (SASRec)
BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations
Contrastive Learning for Sequential Recommendation (CL4SRec)
S3-Rec: Self-Supervised Learning for Sequential Recommendation

literature_context: A strong proposal should isolate short-history user buckets in evaluation (e.g., interactions < 5, 5-10, > 10), compare to SASRec/BERT4Rec/CL4SRec on Recall@K and NDCG@K, and ablate augmentation and pretraining choices on the short-history slice.

instruction: Propose a self-supervised pretraining method for vision that matches DINOv2-class accuracy on ImageNet linear probing while using significantly less compute. Provide datasets, baselines, metrics, and ablations.
bit: State-of-the-art SSL pretraining (DINOv2, MAE, iBOT) requires hundreds of GPU-days even at modest model scales. Most efficiency improvements either trade accuracy or only help small models, which limits practical adoption when compute is constrained.

reference_papers.title: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners (MAE)
Emerging Properties in Self-Supervised Vision Transformers (DINO)
DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision
iBOT: Image BERT Pre-Training with Online Tokenizer

literature_context: A useful proposal should report ImageNet linear probing accuracy, total GPU-hours to convergence, and at least one transfer benchmark (ADE20K segmentation or COCO detection); ablate masking ratio, augmentation, and tokenizer choices.

topic: Calibrated evaluation of open-ended LLM outputs
instruction: Propose a method for evaluating open-ended LLM outputs that reduces judge bias and gives calibrated uncertainty, not just a single preference score. The proposal should be feasible on existing instruction-following or dialogue benchmarks.
bit: Pairwise LLM-as-a-judge systems such as arena-style evaluation are useful, but they can be sensitive to position bias, verbosity bias, model-family bias, and prompt wording. Most leaderboards report point estimates without uncertainty or failure-mode attribution, making small improvements hard to trust.

reference_papers.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
AlpacaEval: An Automatic Evaluator of Instruction-following Models
Chatbot Arena: An Open Platform for Evaluating LLMs by Human Preference

literature_context: Strong proposals should include a calibration protocol, multiple judge families, reverse-order comparisons, human-labeled subsets, confidence intervals or Bayesian ranking, and ablations over prompt, judge model, and answer length controls.

topic: Failure recovery for tool-using LLM agents
instruction: Generate research proposals for making tool-using LLM agents recover from wrong tool calls, malformed tool outputs, and stale intermediate assumptions. Focus on experiments that can be run with synthetic tool environments or small real APIs.
bit: Tool-using agents often treat tool calls as irreversible facts even when a call fails, returns ambiguous data, or produces a value that contradicts the plan. Existing prompting methods encourage tool use but rarely test recovery policies under controlled tool failures.

reference_papers.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs
API-Bank: A Benchmark for Tool-Augmented LLMs

literature_context: A good proposal should define recoverable error categories, inject tool faults, compare ReAct-style prompting, self-reflection, retry policies, and verifier agents, and report task success, unnecessary-call rate, recovery precision, and cost.

instruction: Propose a benchmark or method for evaluating whether LLM-generated scientific code is reproducible beyond passing a single unit test. Include datasets, baselines, metrics, and failure analysis.
bit: LLM coding agents can often produce code that passes shallow tests but fails under changed seeds, dependency versions, hardware, or dataset splits. Scientific code is especially fragile because results depend on statistical variance, hidden preprocessing, and experiment configuration.

reference_papers.title: The Machine Learning Reproducibility Checklist
Papers with Code: A Free Resource for Machine Learning Papers and Code
MLAgentBench: Evaluating Language Agents on Machine Learning Experimentation

literature_context: Useful proposals should require repeated runs, seed sweeps, dependency lockfiles, dataset checksum checks, statistical result comparison, and ablations over test coverage, environment isolation, and agent self-debugging.

topic: Grounded reasoning over charts and scientific figures
instruction: Propose a method for improving or evaluating multimodal models on chart and scientific-figure reasoning where the answer must be grounded in visual evidence. Include public datasets, baselines, metrics, and ablations.
bit: Many chart QA systems answer correctly by exploiting text priors or OCR shortcuts, while failing to localize the plotted evidence or reason over axes, legends, uncertainty intervals, and derived quantities. Standard accuracy hides whether the model actually used the figure.

reference_papers.title: ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning
PlotQA: Reasoning over Scientific Plots
DePlot: One-shot Visual Language Reasoning by Plot-to-Table Translation
MatCha: Enhancing Visual Language Pretraining with Math Reasoning and Chart Derendering

literature_context: A strong proposal should evaluate answer accuracy together with evidence localization, axis/legend parsing, derived-value error, counterfactual chart edits, and ablations over OCR, table reconstruction, and visual encoders.

instruction: Create research proposals for using LLMs to generate causal hypotheses from observational data and literature while avoiding unsupported causal claims. The proposal should include datasets, baselines, metrics, and ablations.
bit: LLMs can produce plausible causal explanations from text, but observational data alone cannot identify many causal effects. Current workflows often mix literature priors, correlations, and causal language without explicit assumptions or falsification tests.

reference_papers.title: DAGs with NO TEARS: Continuous Optimization for Structure Learning
DoWhy: An End-to-End Library for Causal Inference
Causal Discovery from Subsampled Time Series Data by Constraint Optimization

literature_context: Useful proposals should require explicit causal graphs, identification assumptions, negative controls, synthetic data with known ground truth, and comparison against constraint-based, score-based, and LLM-only baselines.

topic: Evaluation of machine unlearning in language models
instruction: Propose a method for evaluating whether an LLM has actually forgotten targeted information while retaining general capability. Include datasets, baselines, metrics, and ablations.
bit: LLM unlearning methods often show reduced accuracy on forget-set prompts, but models may still reveal the same information through paraphrases, multi-hop prompts, or context reconstruction. Retain-set performance also hides localized capability damage.

reference_papers.title: SISA Training: Machine Unlearning with Sharded, Isolated, Sliced, and Aggregated Training
TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs
Who is Harry Potter? Approximate Unlearning in LLMs

literature_context: A strong proposal should test paraphrase robustness, membership inference, extraction attacks, retain-set utility, localized side effects, and compare gradient ascent, preference-based unlearning, data filtering, and model editing baselines.

topic: Quality control for synthetic instruction data
instruction: Generate research proposals for selecting or filtering synthetic instruction data so that it improves downstream LLM performance without amplifying bias, contamination, or shallow task templates.
bit: Synthetic instruction data can cheaply expand training sets, but naive generation often creates redundant, over-formatted, contaminated, or low-diversity examples. Standard filtering by teacher-model score can reinforce the same teacher biases that produced the data.

reference_papers.title: Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions
WizardLM: Empowering Large Language Models to Follow Complex Instructions
Evol-Instruct: Evolutionary Instruction Tuning for Large Language Models

literature_context: Useful proposals should measure task diversity, contamination, bias amplification, downstream generalization, and compare teacher-score filtering, embedding diversity, difficulty estimation, adversarial filtering, and small human-audited subsets.

topic: Federated learning under severe non-IID client data
instruction: Propose a federated learning method that improves personalization and global robustness under severe non-IID client distributions. Include public or simulated datasets, baselines, metrics, and ablations.
bit: FedAvg and many personalization variants degrade when clients differ by label distribution, feature distribution, device constraints, and participation frequency at the same time. Many papers test one heterogeneity axis in isolation, which overstates robustness in realistic deployments.

reference_papers.title: Communication-Efficient Learning of Deep Networks from Decentralized Data (FedAvg)
Federated Optimization in Heterogeneous Networks (FedProx)
Ditto: Fair and Robust Federated Learning Through Personalization
SCAFFOLD: Stochastic Controlled Averaging for Federated Learning

literature_context: A strong proposal should define multi-axis heterogeneity, compare FedAvg, FedProx, SCAFFOLD, and personalized FL baselines, report global accuracy, client-tail accuracy, fairness, communication cost, and ablate client sampling and personalization strength.

topic: Learning from weak labels in medical imaging
instruction: Propose a method for training medical imaging models from weak labels such as reports, coarse image-level tags, or noisy annotations. Include datasets, baselines, metrics, and clinically meaningful ablations.
bit: Medical imaging datasets often have weak or noisy labels derived from reports rather than dense expert annotations. Models can exploit dataset artifacts or report shortcuts and still score well on image-level metrics while failing localization or subgroup robustness.

reference_papers.title: CheXNet: Radiologist-Level Pneumonia Detection on Chest X-Rays with Deep Learning
CheXpert: A Large Chest Radiograph Dataset with Uncertainty Labels and Expert Comparison
Learning from Noisy Labels with Deep Neural Networks: A Survey

literature_context: Useful proposals should include weak-label noise modeling, localization metrics, subgroup evaluation, uncertainty labels, comparison against supervised, MIL, self-supervised, and report-pretraining baselines, and ablations over label noise and annotation budget.

instruction: Propose a machine learning method for climate downscaling that improves local extreme-event prediction while preserving physical consistency and calibrated uncertainty. Include datasets, baselines, metrics, and ablations.
bit: Neural downscaling methods can produce visually plausible high-resolution fields, but they often smooth extremes, violate conservation constraints, or provide poorly calibrated uncertainty. Standard pixel-wise error metrics underweight rare but decision-critical events.

reference_papers.title: DeepSD: Generating High Resolution Climate Change Projections through Single Image Super-Resolution
ClimateBench: A Benchmark Dataset for Data-Driven Climate Projections
FourCastNet: A Global Data-driven High-resolution Weather Model using Adaptive Fourier Neural Operators

literature_context: A strong proposal should evaluate extremes, calibration, spatial coherence, conservation penalties, and transfer across regions; compare statistical downscaling, CNN/U-Net, diffusion, and neural operator baselines with ablations on physical constraints.

instruction: Generate research proposals for active learning in materials discovery where experiments or simulations are expensive and candidate spaces are structured. Include datasets, baselines, metrics, and ablations.
bit: Many materials discovery pipelines optimize surrogate model uncertainty or expected improvement, but uncertainty is often miscalibrated out of distribution and ignores synthesis feasibility. This can waste expensive simulations or lab measurements on candidates that are invalid or redundant.

reference_papers.title: Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Networks for an Accurate and Interpretable Prediction of Material Properties
Matbench: Benchmarking Machine Learning for Materials Science
GNoME: Scaling Deep Learning for Materials Discovery

literature_context: Useful proposals should combine property prediction, uncertainty calibration, diversity, and synthesizability constraints; compare random, Bayesian optimization, deep ensembles, graph neural networks, and active learning acquisition functions on Matbench-style tasks.

instruction: Propose a method for predicting cellular responses to unseen genetic or drug perturbations from single-cell data. Include datasets, baselines, metrics, and ablations.
bit: Single-cell perturbation models often interpolate among observed genes, cell types, or doses but fail under combinatorial or out-of-distribution perturbations. Aggregate expression metrics can hide failures on rare cell states or pathway-specific responses.

reference_papers.title: scGen Predicts Single-Cell Perturbation Responses
CPA: Compositional Perturbation Autoencoder for Single-Cell Response Modeling
scGPT: Towards Building a Foundation Model for Single-Cell Multi-omics

literature_context: A strong proposal should define held-out gene, held-out cell type, and combinatorial perturbation splits; compare autoencoder, graph, and foundation-model baselines; report gene-wise, pathway-wise, and cell-state-specific metrics with uncertainty calibration.

topic: Sim-to-real transfer for language-conditioned robot policies
instruction: Propose a method for improving sim-to-real transfer of language-conditioned robot policies. Include feasible benchmarks, baselines, metrics, and ablations.
bit: Language-conditioned robot policies trained in simulation often fail in the real world because language goals, visual distractors, contact dynamics, and embodiment constraints shift together. Many evaluations report task success without isolating which shift caused failure.

reference_papers.title: RT-1: Robotics Transformer for Real-World Control at Scale
RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control
RoboSuite: A Modular Simulation Framework and Benchmark for Robot Learning
RoboMimic: A Benchmark for Robot Learning from Demonstration

literature_context: Useful proposals should use simulation benchmarks plus a small real or photorealistic validation set, compare behavior cloning, domain randomization, VLA fine-tuning, and failure classifiers, and report success by language, perception, dynamics, and contact-error categories.

topic: Debugging benchmarks for autonomous coding agents
instruction: Create research proposals for evaluating and improving autonomous coding agents on multi-step debugging tasks, not just issue-to-patch success. Include datasets, baselines, metrics, and ablations.
bit: Coding-agent benchmarks often score final patch correctness, but they rarely measure whether the agent localized the fault, formed a correct causal hypothesis, ran useful tests, or avoided masking failures. This makes it hard to improve debugging behavior rather than patch luck.

reference_papers.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
HumanEval: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
Defects4J: A Database of Existing Faults to Enable Controlled Testing Studies for Java Programs

literature_context: A strong proposal should decompose debugging into localization, hypothesis, test selection, patch, and regression checking; compare ReAct agents, planner-executor agents, retrieval baselines, and test-generation agents on SWE-bench-style and controlled fault datasets.
